previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for recurrent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Initial concern included partial bowel obstruction versus severe constipation, with imaging from an outside hospital suggesting either condition. Upon admission, a nasogastric tube was placed but removed after minimal drainage and significant improvement following an enema and bowel movement. The patient's symptoms resolved with supportive care, and he advanced to a regular diet. His diabetes and hypertension were managed with continuation of home medications, and gabapentin was increased for chronic pain. He was discharged home with new prescriptions for Miralax and Colace to prevent recurrence of constipation, with instructions to follow up with his primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ y/o male with multiple medical problems,

floor for several hours when he asked to be discharged. The team 
asked him to remain inpatient for further evaluation but the 
patient insisted on leaving.

hypotension was also of concern given his recent vomiting and 
diarrhea. Vitals were checked in the ED and on the floor and the 
patient was not orthostatic. Blood sugars by finger stick were 
also normal on the floor.

due to his bipolar disorder. Nightfloat reported that he was 
tearful at times but the patient was not noted to be so on the

taking all of his medications as prescribed. He denied any 
homocidial or suicidal ideations.

Lisinopril was continued.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Recurrent seizure.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial CT images were acquired through the head without intravenous
contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted images were also reviewed.

FINDINGS:  There is no intracranial hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or
vascular territorial infarction.  The ventricles and sulci are normal in size
and configuration.  Parafalcine calcifications are stable.  There is no
fracture.  Mastoid air cells are clear.  Imaged paranasal sinuses are also
clear.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial abnormality.

INDICATION:  ___ man with abdominal pain and vomiting.

COMPARISON:  ___.

SUPINE AND LEFT LATERAL DECUBITUS VIEWS OF THE ABDOMEN:  Air is noted within
the stomach, and several loops of bowel, with the largest loop projecting over
the mid abdomen.  Stool and gas are noted in the right colon, and projecting
over the rectum.  Lateral decubitus views demonstrate no suspicious air-fluid
level pattern or evidence of free air. 

Clips are noted in the right upper quadrant.  There is no free intraperitoneal
air.

The visualized lung bases appear clear.

IMPRESSION:  Prominent air-filled loops of bowel in the mid abdomen, with
stool and gas noted in the colon and rectum, without evidence of obstruction.

INDICATION:  ___ man with abdominal pain.

COMPARISON:  ___.

PA AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  Lung volumes are low, resulting in
vascular crowding.  There is no consolidation or pleural effusion.  The heart
size is unchanged.  There is no hilar or mediastinal enlargement.  Pulmonary
vascularity is normal in caliber.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.

INDICATION:  ___ man with severe abdominal pain.  History of Puestow
procedure with Roux-en-Y.  Evaluate for small-bowel obstruction.

COMPARISON:  ___ and ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Intravenous contrast material could not be administered secondary
to inability to obtain venous access.  Oral contrast was administered. 
Multiplanar reformatted images were generated.

CT ABDOMEN WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  At the lung bases, there is dependent
atelectasis bilaterally, without consolidation or pleural effusion.  The heart
size is normal, with a small amount of pericardial fluid.  Coronary artery
calcifications are noted.

In the abdomen, assessment of solid organs is limited in the absence of IV
contrast.  Liver, spleen, adrenal glands, and kidneys are grossly unremarkable
without hydronephrosis.  The patient has undergone prior cholecystectomy and a
pancreaticojejunostomy.  The pancreas itself demonstrates unchanged atrophy
and multifocal calcification compatible with chronic pancreatitis.  The
stomach and duodenum are grossly unremarkable, although underdistended.  The
abdominal aorta and its major branches are grossly unremarkable.  Small lymph
nodes in the retroperitoneum and mesentery do not meet size criteria for
pathologic enlargement.

Focal ventral abdominal wall laxity is slightly more prominent than
previously, without hernia. 

CT PELVIS WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  Oral contrast material has traversed the small
bowel and entered the ascending colon.  There is no bowel obstruction. 
Anastomoses are patent.  Moderate fecal loading is present.  The appendix is
normal.  The urinary bladder and prostate gland are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid in the pelvis.  There is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy by
size criteria.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There is no fracture or worrisome bony lesion.

IMPRESSIONS:
No bowel obstruction or acute intra-abdominal abnormality.
